findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State HOW a run's opening step enumerates the prior run's tickets (e.g. operator supplies the prior-run ticket IDs at invocation, or the run's tickets share a declared discovery-SHA the operator passes in) so attribution is possible WITHOUT the skill holding counter/tag/state.
evidence: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'
'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own, because a skill that exists to remove mechanism must not install any'
AC: 'It introduces no counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own.'
AC: 'That step reports each previous ticket as merged-with-delta or not-merged' — requires an enumerable set of 'the run's tickets' with no stated source
findings.finding: The scoring protocol requires the next run to read 'the previous run's tickets' and sum 'the merged diffs of exactly those,' but the same skill 'introduces no counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own' — the plan specifies no mechanism by which a run can enumerate which tickets belong to a given prior run.
findings.location: The change — modify, not discard: scoring bullet + 'adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own' bullet; AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7
scenarios: An executor implementing the tidying janitor cannot determine how the opening step identifies 'exactly those' tickets from the prior run without some marker, label, or operator-supplied list.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence specifying that the operator (who approves findings one at a time) supplies the prior run's ticket identifiers — anchored by the prior run's discovery SHA — to the opening step; this keeps the attribution external to the skill, consistent with 'no state of its own.'

findings.checklist_item: Name the attribution key the scoring read uses to map each prior-run ticket to its merged diff (e.g. ticket id in the commit/merge record or the tracker's close-commit link), so 'exactly those' is deterministic.
evidence: 'summing the merged diffs of exactly those' presumes a deterministic ticket->commit mapping
ticketization.md:6 files into a 'generic tracker' following project conventions; the skill 'never edits code', so it does not itself author the commit that would carry a back-reference
No stated mechanism (commit trailer, tracker merge record, ticket-id convention) ties a merged diff back to the ticket that declared it
findings.finding: The scoring read must map 'exactly those' previous-run tickets to the specific merged diffs that closed them, but the plan names no attribution key, and the skill files generic-tracker tickets and never edits code, so the diff-to-ticket linkage is left unspecified.
findings.location: The change — 'a run is scored by what LANDED, attributed to the run' bullet
scenarios: Next run opens, lists prior tickets, but cannot deterministically find which merged commits implemented each one because no ticket-id-in-commit (or equivalent) linkage is required

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a tidying run's own tickets are identified for the opening scoring read WITHOUT violating the no-persistent-state / no-tag-vocabulary rule (e.g. the operator supplies the prior run's discovery SHA or ticket ids as the read's input), so 'exactly those' tickets is deterministic.
evidence: Plan: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'
Plan: 'the skill adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own'
Existing grouping mechanism being removed: examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/ticketization.md:10 'Create an epic titled Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>'
A decision rule (attribution read) depends on a schema (how a run's ticket-set is delimited) that is never co-located or defined
findings.finding: The tidying janitor's scoring protocol instructs the next run to read 'the previous run's tickets ... exactly those' and sum their merged diffs, but the plan also forbids the skill from introducing any 'counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own' — and never specifies the mechanism by which a run's own tickets are identified/enumerated. The existing skill relies on a dated 'Janitor Cleanup <YYYY-MM-DD>' epic (ticketization.md:10) to group a run's tickets; removing that grouping without a replacement leaves the scoring step's input set ('exactly those' tickets) undefined.
findings.location: Plan section 'The change — modify, not discard', scoring bullet ('the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets'); AC 'It names the measuring actor and when' and 'It introduces no counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own.'
scenarios: The next run (or operator) runs the opening scoring step and cannot deterministically decide which tickets were filed by the prior tidying run, because the skill left no run-identifying tag/epic/state
Two tidying runs' tickets interleave in the tracker and the scoring read over-counts or under-counts a run's merged deletions
findings.suggested_fix: State that the scoring read takes the prior run's discovery SHA (already recorded on each ticket as the measurement anchor) or an operator-supplied list of the prior run's ticket ids as its input set — not a skill-owned epic or tag — thereby identifying 'exactly those' tickets while honoring the no-state constraint.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the vendor/model token denylist the new neutrality test asserts against (e.g. the specific vendor names, model family names, and tool-calling-syntax tokens), so the test's zero-match assertion is deterministic.
evidence: '`tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py` (new) scans both skill trees for a denylist of vendor and model tokens, asserting zero matches.'
AC: 'Neither skill names a specific model or vendor, proven by the neutrality test named below.'
The denylist is the entire substance of the test; without it the test's pass/fail is undefined.
findings.finding: AC13 is 'proven by the neutrality test named below,' and that test (`tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py`) is NEW and scans 'a denylist of vendor and model tokens,' but the plan never specifies the denylist contents — the load-bearing data is left for the executor to choose.
findings.location: Plan grounding, final command bullet; AC13
scenarios: Two executors author different denylists; one passes an Anthropic-mentioning skill because 'claude' wasn't in the list, the other fails it.
findings.suggested_fix: List the concrete denylist tokens in the plan (vendors and model families to forbid, e.g. gpt/claude/gemini/openai/anthropic plus vendor-specific tool-call syntax markers) so the test is reproducible.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which skill(s) retain each 'never edits code' statement, and make the tidying janitor's posture (files tickets, does not directly edit code) explicit.
evidence: '"Never edits code" is stated three times and all three move with the split: SKILL.md:14 ... :68 ... :127.'
The tidying janitor is described as filing tickets ('each ticket it files declares the deletion'), implying it too does not directly edit code, but this is never stated as the rule's destination.
findings.finding: The plan states the 'never edits code' rule (three occurrences) 'move[s] with the split' but does not say to WHICH skill(s) each moves; both skills file tickets, so it is ambiguous whether the tidying janitor also carries a never-edits-code rule or whether only the defect audit does.
findings.location: Plan grounding, 'Never edits code' paragraph; 'The change' section
scenarios: An executor moves all three never-edits-code statements into only the defect-audit skill, leaving the tidying janitor silent on whether it edits code directly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the success-metric wording with the parent: either note that the per-ticket attribution read SUPERSEDES the operator ruling's 'measured on `main` a week later' phrasing (and amend the parent clause so it stops asserting the main-delta method), or restate the leaf metric in the parent's terms.
evidence: Parent operator ruling: 'a success metric measured on `main` a week later rather than by tickets filed'
Leaf: 'A bare `main`-to-`main` delta cannot score a tidying run: `main` moved +54,961/-26,221 over 114 commits ... so a run's few hundred deleted lines are invisible in it'
Leaf substitutes: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those'
Both forms satisfy the parent's core intent — score by what landed, NOT by tickets filed — so the parent's goal remains intact; only the measurement instrument is redefined.
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the parent's named success-metric mechanism: the operator ruling authorizes a success metric 'measured on `main` a week later', but the leaf explicitly rejects that ('A bare main-to-main delta cannot score a tidying run') and substitutes per-ticket attribution against the run's own tickets.
findings.location: Plan section 'The change — modify, not discard' (attribution bullet) vs parent operator ruling 2026-11-02, deliverable 6
scenarios: A reviewer checking the leaf against the operator's literal authorized wording flags the 'measured on main' phrasing as unmet.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note in the plan grounding that the attribution read realizes the parent's 'not by tickets filed' intent and intentionally replaces the 'measured on `main` a week later' instrument, and raise an amendment to the epic deliverable-6 wording so parent and leaf agree.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how a previous-run ticket that merges AFTER the successor run's opening read is reconciled (e.g. a 'still-open at scoring time' bucket that a later read re-settles), so slow-merging deletions are credited rather than permanently reported 'never merged'.
evidence: 'the NEXT run opens by reading the previous run's tickets and summing the merged diffs of exactly those, reporting lines removed and mechanisms retired against what each declared, plus the ones never merged'
'Scoring is that read, not a privilege of the next run' — the plan frames scoring as one read with an operator fallback, but names no re-scoring of a ticket that lands after that read
Operator approves one finding at a time and tickets are 'landable in one session' — real merge latency means some run-N tickets will still be open when run N+1 opens its scoring read
findings.finding: The attribution-scoring mechanism defines scoring as a single read at the successor run's opening, with no re-scoring step, so a previous-run ticket that merges AFTER the next run opens is permanently reported 'never merged' and its landed deletions are never credited.
findings.location: The change — 'a run is scored by what LANDED' bullet
scenarios: Run N files 5 tickets; operator approves/merges 3 before run N+1 opens and 2 shortly after; run N+1's opening read credits only 3 and marks 2 'never merged'; those 2 are never re-scored even once they land
findings.suggested_fix: Add that the scoring read classifies each prior ticket as merged-with-delta, not-merged-and-closed, or still-open; and that a still-open ticket is re-read (by a later run or the operator) when it lands, rather than being fixed as 'never merged' at first read.

findings.checklist_item: Clarify that check_mechanism_delta.py supplies the seven-kind taxonomy for declaring/scoring retirements (a before/after tree census bracketing the merged diffs), not a per-ticket measurement mode, since the script only offers tree-wide --check/--update-stale.
evidence: check_mechanism_delta.py: --check prints tree-wide 'active/new/increased/stale'; --update-stale drains stale entries — neither attributes retirement to a specific diff or ticket (detect_all/census/_scan_once walk the whole tree)
The dependency ticket fe94 establishes the seven-kind list as a self-contained taxonomy the rubric enumerates inline, suggesting the citation may intend the taxonomy, not a per-diff measurement API
The scoring bullet says the run reports 'mechanisms retired by kind and name' per ticket, which the cited script has no mode to produce per-ticket
findings.finding: The plan cites scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py as the measure of 'mechanisms retired by kind and name', but that script is a whole-tree census against a committed baseline with only --check/--update-stale modes and no per-diff/per-ticket measurement, so it cannot directly report what a given ticket's diff retired; the plan does not disambiguate whether the script is a measurer or only the seven-kind taxonomy source.
findings.location: The change — ticket-declaration bullet, '(the seven the ratchet counts, scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py)'
scenarios: Implementer reads 'measured by scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py' and tries to invoke a per-ticket retirement mode that does not exist, or writes a bespoke per-diff counter the plan's no-new-mechanism principle discourages
